facts.statement: The animal is known only from a partial skull found in Barremian-age rocks of the Vectis Formation on the Isle of Wight.
facts.quote: It is known only from a partial skull recovered from Barremian-age rocks of the Lower Cretaceous Vectis Formation (Wealden Group) of the Isle of Wight.

facts.statement: Its short and wide skull features a eusuchian-like palate and enlarged posterior teeth adapted for crushing.
facts.quote: This skull, BMNH R 177, is short and wide, with a eusuchian-like palate and inferred enlarged posterior teeth that would have been suitable for crushing.

facts.statement: Richard Owen described the genus in 1874, naming Hylaeochampsa vectiana as the type species.
facts.quote: Hylaochampsa was described by Richard Owen in 1874, with H. vectiana as the type species.

facts.statement: Researchers James Clark and Mark Norell classified Hylaeochampsa as the sister group to Crocodylia.
facts.quote: James Clark and Mark Norell positioned it as the sister group to Crocodylia.

facts.statement: Hylaeochampsa is currently recognized as the oldest known unambiguous eusuchian.
facts.quote: Hylaeochampsa is currently the oldest known unambiguous eusuchian.

facts.statement: The animal lived during the Barremian to Aptian stages, approximately 125.77 to 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)
